newsitem.title: FRANCE: Forty pct French wheat bids seen at or near zero.
newsitem.headline: Forty pct French wheat bids seen at or near zero.

text.p: European Union wheat export bids through France on Thursday included 92,000 tonnes at a zero refund or a refund of 0.01 Ecus per tonne -- 40 percent of the total volume sought, grain traders said.
Bids for another 30,000 tonnes went in for refunds up to 0.75 Ecus per tonne, worth $172 to $173 per tonne fob France.
Grain office ONIC earlier reported total bids for 222,000 tonnes between 0.00 Ecus and 6.07 Ecus per tonne.
Traders estimated these included bids for 37,000 tonnes at zero and 55,000 tonnes at 0.01 Ecus.
The cumulative volume of bids up to 0.75 Ecus (including the bids at zero or 0.01 Ecus) was 122,000 tonnes, they said. Cumulative volume reached 142,000 tonnes for bids up to one Ecu.
A refund of zero -- whose value is guaranteed unlike the "nil value" licences now available daily -- prices French wheat around $174 or $175 for May export, traders said.
